gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named testers measured the 1 kWh-class candidates at only about 910–1,030 Wh of usable AC: BLUETTI AC180 950 Wh (OutdoorGearLab) and 1,030 Wh (StorageReview), EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus 910 Wh (StorageReview) and 935 Wh (ADAC), Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 910 Wh (OutdoorGearLab) and 943 Wh (ADAC). ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro gave just 920 Wh (StorageReview) despite its 1,451 Wh label. So a 0.7–1.0 kWh booth day uses up most or all of any of these, and only a 2 kWh unit leaves real reserve.
standout_why: I compared against portableenergylab.com (cited), which names no products and has no measurements, only 'example values for illustration'. I also read voltandvalley.com, which has only maker specs plus an assumed 85% conversion figure. ChatGPT's two answers used maker capacities (1,152 / 1,024 / 1,070 / 768 Wh) and their own estimate of '~870 Wh usable'. Our current page gives 'AC180 950–1,030' and 'S2000 Pro about 920–1,380 in tests' without naming who measured them. It also says 'about 15 W idle' with no source. No page names a tester or a date, and none shows a lab measuring the 1 kWh class side by side. None mentions ADAC's 'mangelhaft' downgrade of the Jackery 1000 v2, which ChatGPT recommended in the plain chat.
decides: This confirms the AC180 as the 1 kWh pick: it measured highest of the 1 kWh units (950–1,030 Wh, against 910–950 for the DELTA 3 Plus and Jackery). It also confirms that the margin is thin for a 0.7–1.0 kWh day. Low loads make it worse: techtest.org got 623 Wh from the AC70 at 50 W AC but 707 Wh at 500 W, and idle draw costs about 8–15 W. This backs the Elite 200 V2 (idle 9.5 W per The Solar Lab) as the pick for running a fridge without worry. The S2000 Pro's 'Yes, with margin' row should be cut: StorageReview measured 920 Wh, and the unit shut off at 22% remaining. Finally, ADAC's safety downgrade of the Jackery 1000 v2 counts against ChatGPT's 'best lightweight' card.
